title: Resumable streaming prefetch adapter with cancellable read-windows for Go SDK
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Implement a resumable prefetch adapter for the Go SDK streaming client that provides better client ergonomics around context cancellation and timeouts. The adapter should allow callers to use short-lived context deadlines for individual Receive/Next calls while the streaming connection (and its network goroutine) continues to prefetch and maintain resume state. Goals: (1) avoid tearing down transport on transient per-call context cancellation, (2) limit memory growth with bounded prefetch windows, (3) expose a simple, cancel-safe API for callers that prefer deadline-scoped reads, and (4) support resume tokens so streams can be rehydrated after transient disconnects.
acceptance_criteria: SDK exposes a new PrefetchStream wrapper that implements the existing streaming interface and accepts per-call contexts without closing the underlying transport when contexts expire.
Prefetch window size is configurable and defaults to a conservative value (e.g., 8 messages). Memory usage remains bounded under stress tests.

When a caller cancels the per-call context, the adapter returns immediately with a context.Canceled/DeadlineExceeded error but continues populating the prefetch buffer in the background so subsequent Resume/Receive can succeed without a new connection when possible.
Resume tokens are surfaced and validated: after a reconnect, the adapter continues delivering items from the correct logical position. Regression tests cover resume semantics.
No behavior change for callers that do not opt into the PrefetchStream wrapper (backwards compatibility).

Comprehensive unit and integration tests (including race detector) pass in CI and a small perf benchmark shows <5% additional CPU overhead at typical load compared to current streaming implementation while improving 99th percentile latency for short-deadline callers.
technical_design: Design summary: add a PrefetchAdapter type that sits between the raw transport stream and the public StreamReceiver. Internally it runs a single background goroutine per logical stream that reads from the transport and appends items to a bounded ring buffer. Receive(ctx) will attempt to read from the buffer first and, if empty, will wait for either an item or the ctx to be done. Important invariants: the background reader uses a stream-level context (ctxStream) with the real connection lifetime; per-call contexts only control the Receive blocking semantics. On reconnect, the adapter uses the last-seen resume token to reinitialize the transport and fills the buffer before returning to callers. To avoid races we use a small set of atomics and a single mutex protecting the buffer head/tail and resume token. The adapter exposes Close() which cancels ctxStream and drains resources.
implementation_notes: API: type PrefetchStream struct { /* implements StreamReceiver */ }
Constructor: NewPrefetchStream(raw StreamReceiver, opts ...PrefetchOpt) where PrefetchOpt allows BufferSize, ReadTimeout, and LeaseRenewInterval
Use a ring buffer with capacity=BufferSize and store minimal per-item metadata (sequence id + resume token + payload ptr) to limit allocations.
Background reader should respect server-provided lease/ack semantics; implement exponential reconnect/backoff with jitter and observe global rate-limit signals from transport.
Per-call Receive(ctx) semantics: if buffer non-empty return next; else select{ case <-ctx.Done(): return ctx.Err(); case item := <-itemCh: return item }
Ensure Close() waits for background goroutine to exit and returns any final error; do not block indefinitely on network shutdown.
Use testing hooks to inject network stalls and forced context cancellations for determinism.
Avoid calling transport.Close() on per-call cancel; only Close() or stream-level failures should close transport.
Add instrumentation points: prefetch_buffer_size_gauge, prefetch_items_total, prefetch_reconnects_total, per_call_cancel_rate.
Document memory trade-offs and recommended BufferSize per workload in SDK README section.
Add a short design doc link: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Prefetch+Adapter+for+Go+SDK (internal).
testing_plan: Unit tests for ring buffer: concurrent write/read, buffer wrap, zero/capacity cases.

Integration test: simulated transport that yields items slowly; assert Receive with short deadline returns context.DeadlineExceeded while buffer still fills in background, and subsequent Receive with new ctx gets buffered items.
Fault injection: cut connection mid-prefetch and verify resume token replays correctly after reconnect.
Race detection: run go test -race across full adapter tests.
Benchmark: compare Receiver.Receive latency distribution before/after adapter under a workload with frequent per-call deadlines.
E2E smoke on staging with dedicated capacity to validate no regressions in production telemetry dashboards.
rollout_plan: Merge behind feature flag: prefetch_adapter=true by default for SDK alpha channel; disabled for stable until GA.
Canary release: enable for 5% of new SDK clients via config flag, monitor per_call_cancel_rate and connection churn metrics.
If metrics stable after 48 hours, increase to 50% then 100% for alpha. For GA, publish migration notes and recommended buffer sizes.
Provide a small cookbook snippet in SDK README showing migration and examples for deadline-based callers.
Coordinate with DEX (developer experience) to update examples and with Support for potential customer questions.
